latin: Operārius quīdam in fabricā lignāriā<sup>1</sup> opus suum faciēbat.
Ita īnscītus<sup>2</sup> is erat ut quōdam diē sibi nāsum serrā mēchanicā<sup>3</sup> stupidē secuerit<sup>4</sup>.
Ā medicō<sup>5</sup> cūrātus, domō<sup>6</sup> tamen exīre nōlēbat: sine nāsō sē rīdiculum vidērī arbitrābātur<sup>7</sup>.
Amīcus bonus nocte domum ejus advēnit, eīque dīxit:
Vēnī mēcum! Ūna ambulābimus<sup>8</sup>. Tē āërem pūrum respīrāre oportet. Nocte nēmō dēfōrmitātem tuam vidēre poterit.
Tibi optō<sup>11</sup> bonam noctem, bonam valētūdinem, bonum vīsum!
Alter respondit: — Propter<sup>12</sup> bonam noctem bonamque valētūdinem tibi grātiās agō. Sed cūr mihi bonum optēs<sup>13</sup> vīsum nōn intellegō.
Tunc amīcus: — Sī bonum vīsum perdās et, exemplī grātia, myops fīās, quōnam oculāria impōnās<sup>14</sup>?
Secuī, secuistī, secuit, secuērunt, secuisse; secuerim, secuerīs, sectus, secta, sectum.
latinAccented: Operā́rius quīdam in fábricā lignā́riā<sup>1</sup> opus suum faciḗbat.
Ita īnscī́tus<sup>2</sup> is erat ut quōdam diē sibi nāsum serrā mēchánicā<sup>3</sup> stúpidē secúerit<sup>4</sup>.
Ā médicō<sup>5</sup> cūrā́tus, domō<sup>6</sup> tamen exī́re nōlḗbat: sine nāsō sē rīdículum vidḗrī arbitrābā́tur<sup>7</sup>.
Amī́cus bonus nocte domum ejus advḗnit, eī́que dīxit:
Vēnī mēcum! Ūna ambulā́bimus<sup>8</sup>. Tē āërem pūrum respīrā́re opórtet. Nocte nēmō dēfōrmitā́tem tuam vidḗre póterit.
Tibi optō<sup>11</sup> bonam noctem, bonam valētū́dinem, bonum vīsum!
Alter respóndit: — Propter<sup>12</sup> bonam noctem bonámque valētū́dinem tibi grā́tiās agō. Sed cūr mihi bonum optēs<sup>13</sup> vīsum nōn intéllegō.
Tunc amī́cus: — Sī bonum vīsum perdās et, exémplī grā́tia, myops fīās, quōnam oculā́ria impṓnās<sup>14</sup>?
Sécuī, secuístī, sécuit, secuḗrunt, secuísse; secúerim, secúerīs, sectus, secta, sectum.
english: A certain worker was doing his job (work) in a carpenter’s (wood-related) workshop.
He was so clumsy (lacking in expertise) that one day (on a certain day) he foolishily cut off his nose with a mechanical saw.
Having been cured by the doctor, he still (however) didn’t want [to leave his house] (to go out from house): without a nose, he thought [he looked] (himself to look) ridiculous.
A good friend came to his house at night and said to him:
Come with me! We shall take a stroll (we-shall-walk) together. You need to breathe (it-is-required you to-breathe) fresh (pure) air. At night no one will be able to see your deformity.
After the walk, the friend said to his friend:
I wish you good night, good health, and good sight.
The other replied: — I thank you on account of the ‘good night’and the ‘good health’. But I don’t understand why you wish (should wish) me (to me) good sight.
Then the friend [said]: — If you should loose your good eyesight and, for example, become short-sighted, upon what would you then rest your spectacles?
I cut, you cut, he/she/it cuts, they cut, to cut.
I cut (past), you cut, he/she/it cut, they cut, to have cut; may I have cut (subj.), may you have cut, having been cut (masc. sing.), having been cut (fem. sing.), having been cut (neut. sing.).

footnotes: Lignarius, a, um, adj., relating to wood; wood itself is lignum, -i, n.
Inscitus, -a, -um, ignorant, skilless. Derived from scio, -is, -ire, to know.
Serrá mechanicá: ablative, complement of means; note that there is no preposition.
Stupidé is an adverb, formed from stupidus, -a, -um. Secuerit is a perfect subjunctive (of secare, to cut), required by the conjunction ut; we shall come back to this later.
A medico: it is an ablative, complement of agent (vid. sup. N 3). But this time we are dealing a person and no longer with a thing: in this case we put in the prepopition a (by).

Domo: unde exis, from where do you come out? Exeo domo, I come out of the house. Redeo Massiliá, I return from Marseilles. The answer to the question unde?, from where?, is put in the ablative without a preposition when we are dealing with a city or with the word domus.

Se ridiculum videri, infinitive clause: subject, se (himself), in the accusative; verb, videri, passive infinitive of video, -es, -ere; predicative attribute, ridiculum, also in the accusative since it agrees with the subject se; and the whole is governed in parallel by the main verb arbitrabatur (imperfect of arbitrari, to think). One can say that the subordinate clause is the direct object of this verb (arbitrari), hence the accusative.
Ambulabo, ambulabis, ambulabit, ambulabimus, ambulabitis, ambulabunt, future of ambulare (ambulo, -as, -are, to walk); uná ablative of una (one), means together.
Post, after (is constructed with the accusative).
Dixi, dixisti, dixit: perfect of dicere (dico, -is, -ere), to say.

Optem, optes, etc., optent is the present subjunctive of optare (ind.: opto, optas, etc., optant; cf. N 11).

In a direct question we normally use the indicative: cur optas?, why do you wish? But in the indirect question, we always use the subjunctive. This is the reason for non intellego cur optes of P 8.

Imponas, as much as perdas and fias are subjunctives having the role of the conditional. This is not a departure from the preceding rule, because the sense requires the subjunctive in this direct question.

latin: Jūlius bonus erat, itaque māter eī crustulum dedit.
Jūlius ita bonus erat ut māter eī crustulum dederit.
Operārius serram mēchanicam īnscītē dūcēbat, itaque nāsus ejus sectus est.
Marius in domum suam nōs invītāvit, sed īnscrīptiōnem scrībere neglēxit.
Unde venīs? — Lutetiā veniō, dē vīcō latīnō.
Quō vadīs? — Id tibi jam in lēctiōne octāvā dīxī: Rōmam vādō.
latinAccented: Jū́lius bonus erat, ítaque māter eī crústulum dedit.
Jū́lius ita bonus erat ut māter eī crústulum déderit.
Operā́rius serram mēchánicam īnscī́tē dūcḗbat, ítaque nāsus ejus sectus est.
Márius in domum suam nōs invītā́vit, sed īnscrīptiṓnem scrī́bere neglḗxit.
Unde venīs? — Lutétiā véniō, dē vīcō latī́nō.
Quō vadīs? — Id tibi jam in lēctiṓne octā́vā dīxī: Rōmam vādō.
english: Julius was (was being) good, and so his mother gave him a pastry.
Julius was so good that his mother gave him a pastry.
The worker was running (was leading) the mechanical saw ineptly (in an unskilled manner), and so his nose was cut off.
The mechanical saw cut off that one’s nose (the nose of that one).
Marius invited us to his house, but neglected to write the address.
Where are you coming from (“whence comest thou”)? — I am coming from Paris, from the Latin quarter.
Where are you going to (“whither goest thou”)? — I already told you that in the eighth lesson: I am going to Rome.
Why shouldn’t you come with us?
